Arrangement & Wave Editor

Zoom

Song — Playlist

MPC2000XL style: each Sequence (above) is one bar of steps + notes. A Song strings sequences together — add them in order, set how many bars each one plays, and the transport runs the chain instead of looping a single sequence. Edit a sequence any time; the playlist just points at it. Using the same SEQ in several steps reuses that one sequence — an edit shows in every step that uses it. For a variation, use ⧉ Duplicate in the rack instead: the copy is fully independent, so changing it never touches the original.
Pattern mode — SEQ 1 loops on its own.
While the song plays, Follow jumps the rack view to each sequence as it’s reached — turn it off to edit a different sequence without the view moving. In Song mode, Export renders the whole playlist chain.

Browser — Sounds

Sound library — pick your folder:
• Windows (OBS PC): your Google Drive for Desktop folder, straight from Drive.
• MacBook Pro: your External Drive / local folder with your sounds copied to it — no Drive for Desktop needed.
Either way the files stay on your machine; the browser only reads the folder you pick.
Click or ↑ ↓ arrow-key a sound to preview it in place; press its Load button and it opens whole in the Chopper at the top of this tab — you chop it with markers, non-destructively. The Crate holds loops & samples only — drum one-shots live in the Drum Machine kits, not here.

    Chopper — slice loops & records

    The Chopper - Non Destructive Sampler sits at the top of this tab. Load a whole song or sample into a Chopper block — from the Crate's per-sound Load buttons at the bottom of the tab, or the block's own Load — drop markers on its wave window, and the regions between them play from the block's keyboard and sequence as notes on the block's own channel. One knob set shapes the whole sample; the source file is never cut.

    Channel Rack

    Sequence Seq Transpose +0 st Bars Shortening never deletes: notes past the end stay in the project and play again when you lengthen it back. Template Click a channel name to select it — sampler, FX & mixer follow the selection. Swap the sample anytime; the pattern never moves.
    Step Sequencer

    Piano Roll — 808

    No note selected — click a note block to select it.
    FL-style editing: click an empty cell to add a note · drag a note to move it (up/down = pitch, auditioned as you drag on pitched channels) · drag its right edge to change its length · right-click or long-press a note to delete it. Drum channels get the same treatment — their step-grid hits show as dashed blocks and become full notes the moment you drag, resize or set their velocity. In-key rows are tinted, roots are gold, out-of-key notes flag red on the 808. Tools (top right of the Piano Roll): Draw is the editing above. Eraser — tap a note to delete it, or drag across a run of notes to clear them all; no long-press needed, which is the reliable way to delete on a phone browser. Splitter — tap a note to cut it in two at the tapped spot, or drag a vertical line across stacked notes to cut every note it crosses at that same column; the cut follows the Snap setting (Snap on = nearest grid line, Snap off = the exact sub-step position tapped), both halves keep the original pitch and velocity, notes too short to split are left alone, and each tap or drag is a single undo step. Select — drag across the grid to marquee-select some or all notes, click a note to select just it, drag any selected note to move the whole selection together (relative positions kept), Delete removes the selection; a group move or delete is one undo step. The grid's lines are the Snap setting — change Snap and the divisions redraw to match. The teal line sweeping the grid in playback is the playhead, and the keyboard under the roll lights each note as it sounds. Voices (top right, beside Root note) is the channel's polyphony: Poly lets notes ring over each other; Mono (the MPC 2000's word) cuts the ringing voice the moment a new note lands — the setting for 808s and sounds that must never overlap. Pitch detection: every sample you assign is analysed and its pitch is reported in the header (⟳ Re-detect re-runs it) — for tuning and the key guide only. Detection never moves a root: every channel's root is C5 unless you move it with the Root Note control, so the same key always plays the same pitch. A chop/loop's detected key sets the project key, and a sound with no clear pitch says so instead of guessing. Key guide (top right) is off unless you call it: on, the project key's scale rows light with the root strongest, out-of-key rows dim, and the keyboard marks its in-key keys — guidance only, nothing is ever blocked.
    Velocity laneDrag a bar to set that note’s velocity (1–127).

    Live input

    —
    Notes trigger channels by the template’s GM map (36 kick · 38 snare · 39 clap · 42 closed hat · 44 pedal · 46 open hat). Other notes play the selected pitched channel. With ● Rec on and the loop playing, hits record into the pattern.

    Export — stems + master

    Format

    Render

    One WAV per channel through its own gain, FX, fader & pan — all the same length, starting at zero, with reverb/delay tails. Master runs through the limiter. Files download to this machine. In Song mode, the playlist chain is rendered end-to-end instead of repeating one sequence.

    Project file

    Save .json (Options tab) carries patterns, templates, mixer, FX and settings — open it on the other machine and keep going. Loaded samples are referenced by name; re-drop the same audio file if a channel shows “sample missing.”
